ratings_why.fun: Reading the shop as a menu of texts makes every turn a fresh puzzle, and the payoffs grow the board, but two layers of text per card slow each look.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because it changes the shop itself: you take a unit's text and leave a Stock in its slot, which no tribe today does and which acts out the changeling tale directly.

verdict_why: Two wording fixes remain (Bee Orchid's 'wears a unit' and how a bare Stock wears); the design itself is ready.

points.text: Bee Orchid says 'each Changeling that wears a unit', but Guise defines 'wears a unit' as the act of putting one on. Say 'that has a guise' if any guise counts, or 'that wore a unit this turn' if only new ones do.
A Stock 'can wear that unit, at most once', but nothing says how without the Alder Whittler or Wicker Moll. Say it is a drag action like Guise, usable once, from board or hand.

The fantasy lands best when the cards act out the tale. A card that uses what changelings dread (eggshells unmasking a guise for a payoff, cold iron) would add the 'unmasked to polite applause' beat, which no card shows yet.
The Porter's '1 tier above their own' sits beside the tier-minus-2 floor; a line saying it raises only the Changeling's own cap would settle which limit it lifts.
The Coat-Peg Steward has no Guise of its own yet gathers guises, so it reads like an odd one out; giving it Guise would let it wear between fights and match the coat-peg image.

standouts.why: The Stock left in the shop slot is the folklore's log in the cradle, made into a 1-gold choice anyone can see.
Pip Unlike's mirror-backwards Pass is a joke the player gets at a glance, with a worked example on the card.
Penny Second turning the real units into blanks is the duchess story in one Start of Combat line.

weakest.why: Grandfer Acorn with three guises is four texts on one card, the hardest board read in the tribe.
Michaelmas Mummers asks you to count tribes across every guise and then hands out random buffs; hard to predict at a glance.
Cradle Foundling is plain Guise on a body; fine as a seed, but nothing of its own to read.

flags.note: Up to four layers of text on one unit; needs a clear UI badge for each guise or it can't be read in a fight.
Wiping up to four enemy texts may feel unfair to the opponent; worth the owner's eye, not a cut.
'Wears a unit' clashes with the Guise rules' meaning of the same words.
